title: Adaptive Auth Connector Failure: Triage and Automated Recovery Playbook
author: Sana Rodriguez
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook describes detection, triage, and automated recovery steps for failures of customer-managed authentication connectors used during enterprise Private and Dedicated onboarding. The procedures target failures that prevent client sessions from establishing streaming (SSE/WebSocket) or authenticated REST requests to Redwood ingress endpoints.

Scope
-----
- Affects enterprise Private (VPC) and Dedicated tenants that integrate a custom OIDC/SAML/JWT verifier or sidecar auth-proxy.
- Applies to production and staging environments where ingress authentication is enforced.
- Does NOT cover: internal Redwood IAM issues, customer-managed identity provider outages (except for diagnostic suggestions).

Goals
-----
1) Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) by providing a deterministic triage path.
2) Provide automated remediation that is safe to run without customer changes where possible.
3) Clarify when to escalate to SRE, Security, or Customer Engineering.

Indicators: What to watch for
--------------------------------
High-confidence signals (automated alert should fire):
- Authentication error rate > 5% for an enterprise tenant over a 5m window AND absolute 5xxs on the ingress proxy > 1%
- Streaming session establishment failures (SSE open failures / WebSocket handshake failures) > 3% for 5m
- Sudden increase in latency for token verification path (token-verify RT 95th percentile increases by >200ms)

Low-confidence signals (use with other signals):
- 401 spike on a single client IP range
- Repeated JWT signature failures with same kid

Severity levels
---------------
- Sev2: >30% auth failures or streaming unavailable for >10% of traffic for >10m. Requires SRE and CS on-call.
- Sev3: 5-30% auth failures or degraded streaming for <30% of traffic for 5-30m. CS primary triage.
- Sev4: <5% auth failures or short blips <5m. Monitor and document.

Quick kill-switch (when to run before full triage)
-----------------------------------------------
If customer-facing production is impacted broadly (Sev2) and immediate remediation is required:
1) Move tenant to fallback auth mode (if enabled) via control-plane toggle. Command:

# curl (internal)
curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood-inference.internal/api/tenants/{tenant_id}/auth/fallback \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"mode":"allow-read-only"}'

2) If fallback is not available, route traffic to a verified backup verifier (see Backup Verifier section).
Note: These actions are disruptive  notify customer, open incident, and run full triage in parallel.

Triage checklist (ordered, try each step until resolved)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm alerts and scope
   - Identify impacted tenant(s) and start an incident channel.
   - Query traffic & auth errors: Prometheus/Insights example:

# PromQL: auth error rate for tenant
sum(rate(ingress_auth_errors_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m])) by (code)

2) Correlate with deployment events
   - Check recent canary/rollout timestamps for ingress-sidecar or control-plane changes in last 60 minutes.
   - Command (internal): gitops status --tenant TENANT123 --since 60m

3) Verify token issuance path
   - If customer uses external IdP: validate IdP token issuance latency and errors. Suggested IdP checks:
     - Okta: /api/v1/logs for token errors in last 5m
     - AzureAD: sign-in logs, conditional access failures

4) Inspect verifier logs
   - Container logs (kubectl or cloud logs): search for signature verification, kid mismatch, and clock skew errors. Example grep:

kubectl logs -n tenant-TENANT123 deployment/auth-verifier --since=15m | egrep 'kid mismatch|signature|clock skew|token expired'

5) Check clock skew and TLS certs
   - Confirm NTP drift < 2s on verifier hosts.
   - Confirm TLS chain validity for verifier to IdP and ingress TLS certs.

6) Streaming-specific checks
   - Inspect connection accept counts on ingress proxies and check for 4xx during handshake.
   - If SSE handshake is failing but REST auth passes, inspect SSE proxy and connection limits.

Automated remediation recipes (safe-by-default)
------------------------------------------------
A) Restart verifier process with rolling backoff (safe):
- Use when logs show transient errors (memory spikes, temporary failures).

kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-verifier -n tenant-TENANT123
# Wait with exponential backoff and validate auth-success-metric returns to baseline

B) Refresh JWKS cache and confirm key rotation handling (idempotent):
- Triggered when 'kid mismatch' or JWKS fetch error is detected.

# internal-control API
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/tenants/TENANT123/auth/jwks/refresh -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN'

C) Automated fallback to short-lived allowlist mode (temporary):
- Only use under approved incident runbooks and with customer consent. This operates by allowing read-only traffic that does not require full verifier validation. Rollback is immediate.

D) Circuit-broken IdP requests caching:
- If IdP is rate-limited/out, enable a limited TTL cache of previously validated tokens for principal UIDs for 60s. This requires a control-plane toggle:

curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/tenants/TENANT123/feature-flags \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' -d '{"auth_token_cache_ttl":60}'

Decision matrix: alert -> automated action
---------------------------------------
- auth_error_rate > 5% AND jwks_fetch_failures > 0 -> trigger JWKS refresh (B) then restart verifier (A).
- streaming_handshake_failures > 3% AND handshake_4xx_count > 1% -> increase SSE connection limit and restart ingress proxy; if still failing -> fallback mode.
- idp_rate_limit_detected -> enable token cache (D) and notify customer.

Ownership & escalation
----------------------
- CS On-call: first responder for Sev3/Sev4. Responsibilities: customer comms, initial triage, run automated recipes (A/B).
- SRE On-call: engage for Sev2 or if rolling restart does not restore auth within 10m. Responsibilities: ingress proxy restarts, scaling, and network debugging.
- Security/Identity Engineering: engage when signature mismatches, unusual key rotations, or suspected credential compromise.

Telemetry queries and dashboards (examples)
-----------------------------------------
- Auth error rate (per-tenant):
  sum(rate(ingress_auth_errors_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(ingress_requests_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m]))
- JWKS fetch latency: histograms under jwks_fetch_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}
- SSE handshake failures: sum(rate(sse_handshake_failures_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT123\"}[5m]))

Configuration checklist (table)
------------------------------
- Required items to validate during onboarding:
  - OIDC metadata URL reachable from verifier hosts
  - JWKS TTL configured >= 60s and <= 24h
  - Control-plane fallback mode enabled (boolean)
  - Token cache feature flag available for tenant
  - Ingress proxy connection limit documented per tenant

Suggested commands and scripts
------------------------------
- Run a single-step verifier restart and validate with synthetic:

#!/bin/bash
TENANT=TENANT123
set -e
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-verifier -n tenant-$TENANT
sleep 20
curl -s -I -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN\" https://ingress.$TENANT.api.redwood-inference.com/health | head -n 1

Communication templates
-----------------------
- Short customer update (on Sev3):
  \"We've detected intermittent authentication failures for your tenant between 14:12-14:27 UTC. Our team is performing controlled restarts of the auth verifier and monitoring traffic. No action required on your side. We will update in 30 minutes or on resolution.\"

- Escalation to SRE (on Sev2):
  \"Sev2: Tenant TENANT123 experiencing >30% auth failures since 14:10 UTC. CS has toggled fallback mode. Request SRE to investigate ingress proxy logs, restart proxy if needed, and confirm NTP/TLS state. Incident channel: #inc-TENANT123-auth\"

Unsafe actions (do NOT run without Security)
-------------------------------------------
- Disabling signature checks globally.
- Rolling back customer-managed verifier config to a prior secret without owner consent.

Post-incident checklist
-----------------------
1) Collect verifier logs, JWKS fetch traces, and control-plane toggles.
2) Run root-cause analysis template and attach to incident.
3) Review whether automated remediation should be adjusted (thresholds, timers).
4) Schedule customer-facing RCA if customer impacted beyond SLA.

Appendix: Example incident timeline template
-------------------------------------------
- 14:05: Alert fired (auth_error_rate 7%)
- 14:07: CS created incident channel #inc-TENANT123-auth
- 14:09: JWKS refresh (automated) triggered
- 14:12: Rolling restart auth-verifier initiated
- 14:18: Error rate dropped to 1.2%
- 14:25: Fallback toggles reverted; monitoring for 30m
